<!-- Generated by cargo xtask guide-check --write-reference. Do not edit. -->

The commands the engine accepts. The command line and the assistant server use the same list.

| Command | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `design.summary` | A short summary of the design for people and assistants: counts, board, nets, parts, findings. Read it first; it is far smaller than inspect_design |  |
| `project.rename` | Rename the current project | `name` |
| `project.replace` | Find text across the project and replace it in one call: component references, values and fields, net names, free board and schematic text, and graphic text; a dry run reports every hit without changing anything | `dry_run` (optional), `replace`, `scope` (optional), `search` |
| `project.set_meta` | Record a project metadata entry such as title, revision, company or notes, keyed by 1 to 32 lowercase alphanumeric bytes; recording the same value again is refused | `key`, `value` |
| `project.clear_meta` | Remove one project metadata entry by key | `key` |
| `parameter.set` | Record a named numeric parameter, or change one, and re-run the commands that reference it: holes and vias whose size or position follows the name are written again inside the same undoable step, and a value that breaks one of them is refused and changes nothing. Names are 1 to 32 letters, digits or underscores starting with a letter or underscore | `name`, `note` (optional), `value` |
| `parameter.remove` | Forget a named parameter; while objects still follow it the call is refused and names them, unless unbind is set to release them first | `name`, `unbind` (optional) |
| `parameter.list` | List the project's named numeric parameters with their values, notes and the object fields that follow each one |  |
| `project.set_unit` | Record the unit this design is read in: millimetres, mils or inches. Stored coordinates stay millimetres; inch drill and gerber fabrication output converts to inches, and the recorded unit is reported in the board statistics | `unit` |
| `project.export_archive` | Write the whole design, including its attached text files, to a self-contained archive file that a colleague can open without any other project files | `path` |
| `project.import_archive` | Open a self-contained archive file written by the export, replacing the current project; the replacement is undoable | `path` |
| `component.add` | Place an original built-in symbol: resistor, capacitor, led or connector | `kind`, `position`, `reference` (optional), `rotation` (optional), `value` (optional) |
| `component.place_library` | Place a symbol package with independently movable units and embedded definitions | `path`, `position`, `reference` (optional), `rotation` (optional), `symbol`, `value` (optional) |
| `graphic.group` | Group two to 512 drawn graphics into one unit that can be moved together; each graphic joins at most one group | `graphics` |
| `graphic.ungroup` | Dissolve a graphic group again, leaving its member graphics exactly where they are | `id` |
| `graphic.translate` | Move every graphic in a group by the same offset in one undoable step | `delta`, `id` |
| `dimension.add` | Draw a linear dimension between two points: witness lines, the dimension line offset to one side, and the measured distance in millimetres as text; the pieces are grouped so the whole annotation moves as one unit | `end`, `layer`, `offset` (optional), `start` |
| `dimension.set` | Re-measure an existing linear dimension to new ends or a new offset; the grouped witness lines, dimension line and text update in place | `end` (optional), `id`, `offset` (optional), `start` (optional) |
| `dimension.radius` | Measure a circle or arc: a witness circle, a leader from the centre to a point on the rim, and the radius in millimetres as an R label; the pieces are grouped so the whole annotation moves as one unit | `center`, `layer`, `point` |
| `dimension.diameter` | Measure a circle across its centre: a witness circle, a leader from the far rim through the centre to the near rim, and the diameter in millimetres as a label; the pieces are grouped so the whole annotation moves as one unit | `center`, `layer`, `point` |
| `footprint.assign` | Assign a top-side SMD or plated through-hole footprint with matching physical pins | `id`, `path` |
| `footprint.assign_pattern` | Assign one footprint file to every component whose reference matches a * or ? pattern; components whose pins do not match the pads are skipped and reported | `path`, `pattern` |
| `footprint.assign_table` | Apply a table of reference-to-footprint-file rows, exactly as a footprint assignment CSV exports them, in one undo step; rows whose pins do not match the pads are skipped and every row is reported as assigned, skipped or not found | `rows` |
| `footprint.assign_file` | Read a footprint assignment text file of reference-to-footprint-file rows, as assignment exports write them, and apply every row in one undo step, reporting each row as assigned, skipped or not found | `path` |
| `footprint.refresh` | Refresh every placed component that carries a package, in one undo step, so library edits propagate: give a library nickname to re-read that linked folder's file, or a project library footprint name to apply the edited project copy; components whose pins no longer match the pads are skipped and reported | `library` (optional), `name` (optional) |
| `component.move` | Move a schematic component; connected wire endpoints follow | `id`, `position`, `unit` (optional) |
| `component.rotate` | Set schematic component rotation in degrees | `degrees`, `id`, `unit` (optional) |
| `component.mirror` | Mirror a placed symbol left-to-right or top-to-bottom about its own origin | `axis`, `id` |
| `component.value` | Change the component value | `id`, `value` |
| `component.reference` | Rename a component's reference designator; the new name must be unique | `id`, `reference` |
| `components.reannotate` | Renumber component references in placement order (top to bottom, left to right): optionally restrict to one letter prefix, choose the starting number, and dry-run to preview the mapping; any collision with a reference outside the renumbered group refuses the whole call | `dry_run` (optional), `prefix` (optional), `start` (optional) |
| `part.attach_source` | Record where a part came from on a placed component in one step: manufacturer, part number, datasheet link and the distributor's own order number are written as named properties (Manufacturer, MPN, Datasheet, and one property per distributor ending in SKU) | `datasheet` (optional), `distributor` (optional), `id`, `manufacturer`, `mpn`, `sku` (optional) |
| `component.field` | Set one named component property (datasheet, manufacturer, custom note), or clear it when value is null or omitted | `id`, `key`, `value` (optional) |
| `component.find` | Find components by reference wildcard, exact value or kind; * matches any run of characters and ? matches one | `kind` (optional), `reference` (optional), `value` (optional) |
| `footprint.find` | Find placed footprints by component reference wildcard, exact component value, or lock state; * matches any run of characters and ? matches one | `locked` (optional), `reference` (optional), `value` (optional) |
| `net.create` | Create a named logical net | `name` |
| `net.rename` | Rename an existing net; the new name must be unique | `id`, `name` |
| `net.unroute` | Rip up the routed copper of one net: every track and via carrying that net leaves the board in a single undo step, while the net, its pads and its unrouted connection stay | `net` |
| `net.tie` | Merge two nets into one: every pin, wire, label, track, via and zone on the source net joins the target net, net class and clearance pair memberships follow, and the source net is removed | `source`, `target` |
| `net.swap` | Exchange the names of two nets; each net keeps its id, members and copper, so two nets that crossed during a reassignment can be corrected in one step | `id_a`, `id_b` |
| `pins.set_all_no_connect` | Flag every pin of one component that is neither wired nor assigned, in a single undo step; pins already flagged are skipped | `component` |
| `pins.clear_all_no_connect` | Remove every no-connect flag of one component in a single undo step | `component` |
| `net.set_length` | Set a target routed length and tolerance for one net, or clear the target by omitting it; nets in a class follow their own target when they have one | `id`, `target` (optional), `tolerance` (optional) |
| `net.connect` | Assign unassigned or same-net component pins to a net | `net`, `pins` |
| `net.disconnect` | Take component pins out of a net, clearing their placed pads as well | `net`, `pins` |
| `copper.set_net` | Move an existing track, via or copper zone onto a different net | `id`, `net` |
| `netclass.add` | Create a net class with a clearance requirement, a default track width and optional member nets | `clearance`, `name`, `nets` (optional), `width` |
| `netclass.assign` | Move a net into a net class, or out of every class when the class is null | `class` (optional), `net` |
| `netclass.width_rules` | Set the smallest and largest track width a net class allows; omitted bounds stay as they were | `class`, `max_width` (optional), `min_width` (optional) |
| `netclass.length_rules` | Set the target routed length and tolerance a net class demands; omitted values stay as they were | `class`, `length_tolerance` (optional), `target_length` (optional) |
| `netclass.stub_rules` | Set the longest dead-end copper branch a net class allows; null clears the limit | `class`, `max_stub` (optional) |
| `netclass.clearance` | Change the clearance a net class requires between its copper and everything else | `class`, `clearance` |
| `netclass.set` | Rename a net class, change routing defaults, via size, or differential-pair defaults, with the class rules echoed back | `class`, `name` (optional), `pair_gap` (optional), `pair_width` (optional), `via_diameter` (optional), `via_drill` (optional), `width` (optional) |
| `netclass.remove` | Delete a net class and return its nets to the board default rules | `class` |
| `netclass.assign_pattern` | Move every net whose name matches a wildcard pattern into a net class in one step; * matches any run of characters and ? matches one | `class`, `pattern` |
| `netlist.import` | Import a netlist table: assign listed pins to named nets by reference, creating missing nets | `nets` |
| `netlist.export` | Export the connectivity table: every net with its pins by reference, plus unconnected pins | `net` (optional) |
| `netlist.import_session` | Import net assignments from a Specctra session file on disk: every named net with pins is created if missing and its REF-PIN entries are assigned to matching component pins | `path` |
| `library.link` | Add or update a project library table entry mapping a short nickname to the folder that holds library files, so library commands can address nickname/file without a machine-specific folder | `name`, `path` |
| `library.unlink` | Remove a project library table entry by nickname; the paths it served stop resolving | `name` |
| `padstack.define` | Define or replace a named reusable pad shape: copper shape and size with an optional drill, ready for any placed pad to adopt | `drill` (optional), `height`, `name`, `rounding` (optional), `shape`, `width` |
| `padstack.remove` | Remove a named padstack from the design; pads already shaped by it keep their copper | `name` |
| `padstack.rename` | Rename a defined padstack in place; pads already shaped by it keep their copper, and the new name must still be free | `name`, `new_name` |
| `padstack.duplicate` | Copy a defined padstack under a fresh name, same copper and drill, ready to reshape other pads without touching the original | `name`, `new_name` |
| `padstack.report` | Report every defined padstack with its copper and drill, which placed pads carry it, and which stacks no pad uses, so unused stacks can be tidied away; reads the design without touching it |  |
| `footprint.set_pad_stack` | Reshape one placed pad to a named padstack: copper shape and size, and drill plus plated through-hole conversion when the stack carries a drill | `id`, `pad`, `stack` |
| `dxf.import` | Import a DXF drawing from disk as board graphics (lines, arcs, circles, polylines and text); with use_outline a closed Edge polyline also traces the board outline and the whole drawing shifts to the first quadrant | `path`, `use_outline` (optional) |
| `svg.import` | Import an SVG drawing from disk as board graphics (lines, polylines, polygons, rectangles, circles, simple paths and text, in millimetres with the page flipping y up); with use_outline a closed polygon also traces the board outline and the whole drawing shifts to the first quadrant | `path`, `use_outline` (optional) |
| `wire.connect` | Connect two pins; infer their existing net or atomically create a net if neither is assigned | `from`, `net` (optional), `to` |
| `wire.draw` | Draw a free-form schematic wire with explicit vertices, optionally bound to a net | `net` (optional), `points` |
| `wire.split` | Split a drawn wire into two at a point on one of its segments | `at`, `id` |
| `wire.add_point` | Insert a vertex into a drawn wire at any position along it, extending either end | `id`, `index`, `position` |
| `wire.remove_point` | Remove one vertex from a drawn wire, shortening it or straightening a corner | `id`, `index` |
| `wire.move` | Slide a drawn wire by a distance; junctions sitting on its vertices travel with it | `delta`, `id` |
| `wire.set_point` | Drag one vertex of a drawn wire to a new position, bending or straightening it; refused if a junction would be left off the wire | `id`, `index`, `position` |
| `graphic.add` | Add a free-standing schematic or board graphic: line, rect, circle, arc, polygon or text | `layer`, `points`, `shape`, `text` (optional), `width` |
| `graphic.move` | Translate an existing schematic or board graphic by a delta | `delta`, `id` |
| `graphic.rotate` | Rotate an existing schematic or board graphic in 90-degree steps about its centre or a given pivot | `around` (optional), `degrees`, `id` |
| `schematic.cleanup` | Tidy the schematic in one undoable step: merge junctions that repeat the same net at the same point, drop vertices where a wire repeats itself or runs straight through, and leave any vertex a junction still depends on exactly where it is |  |
| `schematic.new_sheet` | Add a named schematic page; every component lives on exactly one page and sheet 0 is the root page every design starts with | `name` |
| `schematic.rename_sheet` | Rename a schematic page; the new name must differ from every other page name | `id`, `name` |
| `schematic.remove_sheet` | Remove a schematic page; while the page still holds components a move_to destination (another page or the root page 0) is required, and the components keep their positions when they move | `id`, `move_to` (optional) |
| `schematic.move_component` | Move a component to another schematic page, sheet 0 being the root page; its position never changes | `id`, `sheet` |
| `schematic.place_port` | Place a named hierarchy port for a net on a schematic page; a port name already used on another page must carry the same net, which is how a net is handed between pages | `name`, `net`, `position`, `sheet` |
| `schematic.move_port` | Move a hierarchy port to another position, another page, or both at once; a port moved onto a page that already carries its name is refused | `id`, `position` (optional), `sheet` (optional) |
| `schematic.rename_port` | Rename a hierarchy port so a page hands its net under a better name; the net travels with the port, and a new name already used on the same page or carrying a different net on another page is refused | `id`, `name` |
| `schematic.remove_port` | Remove a hierarchy port; the net itself is untouched | `id` |
| `schematic.import_sheet` | Import a sheet file from disk as a new schematic page: components built from the built-in symbol templates with their positions, rotations and properties, and hierarchy ports that join existing nets by name | `name` (optional), `path` |
| `graphic.scale` | Scale a graphic about an anchor point by a factor from 0.01 to 100; the stroke width follows the factor unless keep_width is set | `around` (optional), `factor`, `id`, `keep_width` (optional) |
| `graphic.to_track` | Convert a drawn line or polyline into copper tracks, one segment per vertex pair, on a chosen net and layer; the graphic is replaced by the copper, and the width follows the stroke unless given | `id`, `layer` (optional), `net`, `width` (optional) |
| `plot.to_schematic` | Plot the copper of one layer onto the schematic as editable drawing graphics (tracks become lines, vias become circles and board text joins the plot), shifted so the board origin lands on a chosen sheet point; the copper itself is untouched | `include_text` (optional), `layer`, `origin` (optional) |
| `graphic.set` | Change an existing graphic's layer, stroke width or radius, or its text; omitted fields stay as they were | `id`, `layer` (optional), `text` (optional), `width` (optional) |
| `graphic.set_point` | Move one vertex of an existing graphic to a new position | `id`, `index`, `position` |
| `barcode.place` | Draw a Code 39 barcode of up to 48 characters as bar graphics at a position, with optional height in millimetres, module width in millimetres and layer | `height` (optional), `layer` (optional), `module` (optional), `position`, `text` |
| `schematic.table` | Draw a parts table on the schematic at a position: one row per component sorted by reference, one column per property key (reference and value by default), as ordinary graphics that capture the design as it stands now | `fields` (optional), `max_rows` (optional), `position` |
| `label.place` | Place a local, global, hierarchical or power label, or a junction, naming an existing net | `kind`, `net`, `position`, `rotation` (optional) |
| `wire.draw_bus` | Draw a multi-net bus wire from explicit vertices and label its first vertex with the bus notation; the name is stem*count, like DB*8 naming DB0 through DB7, and member nets that do not exist yet are created in the same step | `name`, `points` |
| `label.place_bus` | Place a bus label at a point naming a group of nets with stem*count notation, like DB*8 for DB0 through DB7; member nets that do not exist yet are created in the same step | `name`, `position`, `rotation` (optional) |
| `label.set_bus` | Rename a bus label in place to a new stem*count notation, like widening DB*8 to DB*16 or refitting it to another group; its point and angle stay put, numbered member nets that do not exist yet are created in the same step, and the nets it named before remain untouched | `id`, `name` |
| `label.move` | Move an existing net label, global label or junction to a new position | `id`, `position` |
| `label.rotate` | Rotate an existing label, global label or power label in degrees | `degrees`, `id` |
| `label.set` | Retype a net label or point it at a different net in place; junctions must stay on matching wire | `id`, `kind` (optional), `net` (optional) |
| `pin.no_connect` | Mark a pin intentionally unconnected, suppressing its unconnected-pin violation | `pin` |
| `board.hole_place` | Drill an unplated through hole at a position: mounting or clearance drills carry no copper and belong to no net | `diameter`, `position` |
| `hole.slot` | Route an unplated mounting slot between two centres: width is the drill diameter, length runs centre to centre plus that width | `end`, `start`, `width` |
| `board.fiducial_place` | Place an optical assembly mark: a bare copper disc the pick-and-place camera locates the board by, on either copper layer | `diameter`, `layer` (optional), `position` |
| `board.fiducial_move` | Move a fiducial mark to a new position | `id`, `position` |
| `board.fiducial_set` | Resize a fiducial mark, move it to the other copper layer, or both at once; the mark keeps its identity and its place in the pick-and-place file, so a panel tune or a back-side build adjusts the existing mark instead of replacing it | `diameter` (optional), `id`, `layer` (optional) |
| `board.fiducial_remove` | Remove a fiducial mark | `id` |
| `board.nettie_place` | Place a net tie: two touching round pads bridging exactly two named nets, the single controlled crossing between split planes | `diameter`, `net_a`, `net_b`, `position`, `rotation` (optional) |
| `board.nettie_move` | Move a net tie and optionally turn its pad axis | `id`, `position`, `rotation` (optional) |
| `board.nettie_set` | Re-aim a net tie: change which two nets it bridges, resize its pads, or both at once; the bridge keeps its identity and its place in the fabrication layers, so a plane split revised during layout retargets the existing tie instead of replacing it | `diameter` (optional), `id`, `net_a` (optional), `net_b` (optional) |
| `board.nettie_remove` | Remove a net tie | `id` |
| `board.hole_move` | Move a drilled unplated hole to a new position; its diameter is kept | `id`, `position` |
| `board.hole_set_size` | Resize the drill of an unplated hole in millimetres; for a slot this is its width | `diameter`, `id` |
| `hole.slot` | Route an unplated slot: a capsule drill from one centre to another at the given width, at least 0.01 mm and at most 50 mm between the centres | `end`, `start`, `width` |
| `pattern.repeat` | Step and repeat holes and cutouts into a grid: every named object is copied at each column and row offset, row by row, and each copy is an independent object | `columns`, `dx`, `dy`, `ids`, `rows` |
| `board.notch` | Cut a rectangular notch out of one straight board outline edge: four corners are inserted so checks, plots and routing all see the new rim | `at`, `depth`, `segment`, `width` |
| `board.datum_add` | Add a named mounting datum for enclosure tools, at a position or at the centre of a drilled hole it then follows | `hole` (optional), `name`, `position` (optional) |
| `board.datum_move` | Move a datum to a new position; a datum tied to a hole is released from it | `id`, `position` |
| `board.datum_rename` | Rename a datum | `id`, `name` |
| `board.datum_remove` | Remove a datum | `id` |
| `via.place` | Place a plated via on an existing net. It joins front and back copper unless from_layer and to_layer limit it to a blind or buried span the board allows; size defaults from the net class when omitted | `diameter` (optional), `drill` (optional), `from_layer` (optional), `net`, `position`, `to_layer` (optional) |
| `via.move` | Move a placed via to a new position; geometry and net are kept | `id`, `position` |
| `via.stitch` | Fill a rectangular area with a grid of stitched vias on an existing net | `bounds`, `diameter`, `drill` (optional), `net`, `spacing` (optional) |
| `zone.place` | Place a poured copper zone: a closed polygon of copper on one layer bound to an existing net | `layer` (optional), `net`, `outline` |
| `zone.move` | Translate a poured zone by a delta; outline and every cutout move together | `delta`, `id` |
| `zone.set_layer` | Move a poured zone, with all its cutouts, to the other copper layer without moving its outline | `id`, `layer` |
| `zone.set_net` | Re-bind a poured zone to another existing net in place; the outline, cutouts, layer and fill state stay put | `id`, `net` |
| `zone.set_point` | Move one vertex of a poured zone's outline, or of one of its cutouts, by index; closing vertices stay paired | `cutout` (optional), `id`, `index`, `position` |
| `zone.insert_point` | Insert a new vertex into a poured zone's outline, or one of its cutouts, at an index; outlines hold 3 to 256 vertices | `cutout` (optional), `id`, `index`, `position` |
| `zone.remove_point` | Remove one vertex from a poured zone's outline, or one of its cutouts, by index; at least three vertices must remain | `cutout` (optional), `id`, `index` |
| `zone.set_fill` | Pour a zone's copper back in, or take it out to a bare outline that carries no copper and reports no findings | `filled`, `id` |
| `zone.fill` | Report the copper a zone actually pours on its layer: area, connected pieces, thermal spokes that reach the fill, pads left starved, detached islands and how many the settings removed, with knockouts round foreign copper, keepouts and the board edge already applied | `id` |
| `zone.pour` | Set how a zone pours: whether plated pads and vias join solid, through thermal spokes or not at all, the relief gap, spoke width and count, the narrowest copper it keeps, and whether detached copper is kept or dropped | `id`, `island_area` (optional), `islands` (optional), `min_width` (optional), `pad_connect` (optional), `relief_gap` (optional), `spoke_width` (optional), `spokes` (optional), `via_connect` (optional) |
| `zone.cutout` | Add a closed cutout outline that removes copper from an existing zone | `outline`, `zone` |
| `symbol.refresh` | Re-read a symbol from its library file and refresh every placed component that carries it, in one undo step, so symbol artwork and pin geometry edits propagate; components whose pin numbers or units no longer match are skipped and reported | `path`, `symbol` |
| `teardrop.add` | Grow teardrop copper where tracks meet pads and vias so junctions survive etching and hand soldering; filter by net or layer, and junctions that already have a teardrop are left alone | `depth` (optional), `layer` (optional), `net` (optional) |
| `teardrop.remove` | Take teardrop copper away again from every junction it was grown on, optionally filtered by net or layer | `layer` (optional), `net` (optional) |
| `board.sync` | Reconcile schematic components and pin nets into PCB footprints; retain placements and report unassigned library symbols |  |
| `board.unroute` | Rip up every track and via on the board in one undo step, leaving pads, zones, text and all nets' connectivity in place |  |
| `track.cleanup` | Remove dangling track stubs, merge collinear same-net segments on one layer, and drop zero-length pieces in one undo step | `layer` (optional), `net` (optional) |
| `board.resize` | Set rectangular board dimensions, in millimetres | `height`, `width` |
| `board.rules.set` | Set the board default copper clearance and recorded fabrication minimums in millimetres | `clearance` (optional), `edge_routed` (optional), `edge_vscore` (optional), `hole_to_copper_npth` (optional), `hole_to_copper_pth` (optional), `hole_to_copper_via` (optional), `hole_to_hole_pad` (optional), `hole_to_hole_via` (optional), `mask_dam` (optional), `max_aspect_ratio` (optional), `min_drill` (optional), `min_npth` (optional), `min_ring_pth` (optional), `min_ring_via` (optional), `min_space` (optional), `min_track` (optional), `plating_allowance` (optional), `preset` (optional), `retrieved` (optional), `silk_line` (optional), `silk_text_height` (optional), `silk_to_pad` (optional), `source_url` (optional) |
| `board.cutout.add` | Add a dimensioned circular Edge.Cuts cutout strictly within the board | `center`, `radius` |
| `board.cutout.move` | Move an existing board cutout to a new centre, keeping it inside the board | `center`, `id` |
| `board.cutout.resize` | Change the radius of an existing board cutout, keeping it inside the board | `id`, `radius` |
| `footprint.move` | Move a board footprint; existing routed tracks stay fixed | `id`, `position` |
| `footprint.rotate` | Set footprint rotation in degrees; existing tracks stay fixed | `degrees`, `id` |
| `footprint.set_pad` | Reposition a placed footprint pad by its local offset, and resize it when it is a plain round pad; shaped pads keep their library shape | `diameter` (optional), `id`, `offset` (optional), `pad` |
| `footprint.set_castellated` | Flag one placed footprint pad castellated - plated and cut at a board edge so another board can be soldered onto it - or clear the flag | `id`, `on`, `pad` |
| `footprint.dock_edge` | Slide a placed footprint along one axis so its copper sits flush against the named board edge, as an edge connector should; rotation is preserved | `edge`, `id` |
| `footprint.set_locked` | Lock or unlock a placed footprint; a locked footprint refuses move, rotate, mirror, array and edge docking until it is unlocked again | `id`, `locked` |
| `footprint.array` | Step-and-repeat: clone a placed footprint and its component into a rectangular grid of copies at fixed column and row spacing; every copy gets fresh IDs and a numbered reference, the clones must stay within the project object limit, and one undo removes the whole array | `columns`, `dx`, `dy`, `footprint`, `rows` |
| `track.add` | Add a straight copper segment; checks report clearance errors rather than hiding them | `end`, `layer` (optional), `net`, `start`, `width` (optional) |
| `track.add_arc` | Add a curved copper segment through three points (start, a point on the curve, end); clearance checks sample the arc and fabrication output draws a true arc | `end`, `layer` (optional), `mid`, `net`, `start`, `width` (optional) |
| `track.straighten` | Turn a curved track back into the straight segment between its ends | `id` |
| `track.set_arc` | Bend an existing track into a circular arc through a new midpoint, straight or already curved alike; the ends, width, layer and net stay put and only the curve changes, so a routed run can swing around an obstacle without being ripped up and redrawn | `id`, `mid` |
| `track.split` | Split one copper segment into two at a point on the track | `at`, `id` |
| `track.chamfer` | Cut the corner between two joined same-net track segments with a diagonal segment | `a`, `b`, `size` |
| `track.set_width` | Change the width of an existing track segment | `id`, `width` |
| `track.set_layer` | Move an existing track segment to the other copper layer without moving its ends | `id`, `layer` |
| `track.set_width_net` | Set the copper width of every track segment on one net in a single step, so a whole net can be thickened or thinned at once; reports how many segments changed | `net`, `width` |
| `track.set_layer_net` | Move every track segment of one net to the other copper layer in a single step, optionally only those currently on a given layer; reports how many segments moved | `from_layer` (optional), `layer`, `net` |
| `track.set_end` | Drag one end of an existing track to a new position, shortening, lengthening or re-aiming it; the other end stays put | `end`, `id`, `position` |
| `via.set_size` | Change the pad and drill diameters of an existing via | `diameter`, `drill` (optional), `id` |
| `via.set_span` | Change which copper layers an existing via joins, making it through, blind or buried; the span must be one the board allows | `from_layer` (optional), `id`, `to_layer` (optional) |
| `via.set_covering` | Set how one via is protected under the solder mask (open, tented, tented_covered, plugged, plugged_covered, filled, filled_covered, filled_capped, named after the seven via protection types); omit covering to follow the board default. Anything but open needs a drilled hole | `covering` (optional), `id` |
| `via.allow_span` | Allow or forbid one extra via span on this board, such as a buried span the fabricator offers; forbidding is refused while a via uses the span | `allow`, `from_layer`, `to_layer` |
| `board.set_via_covering_default` | Set the covering every via follows unless it has its own: open, tented, tented_covered, plugged, plugged_covered, filled, filled_covered or filled_capped | `covering` |
| `track.move` | Translate an existing copper segment by a delta; both ends move together | `delta`, `id` |
| `track.route` | Connect a same-net pad or point to another on the chosen copper layer. Default mode orthogonal is one right-angle bend with no obstacle checks. Mode octilinear routes 45-degree copper around other nets' pads, tracks and cutouts. Mode octilinear_shove walks around pads and cutouts and pushes other nets' tracks aside within fixed iteration limits. Refusals say why and change nothing. Single layer, no vias | `from`, `layer` (optional), `mode` (optional), `net` (optional), `to`, `width` (optional) |
| `track.route_pair` | Route both nets of a declared differential pair between two pad pairs on the chosen copper layer with coupled geometry at the pair gap; corners are cut at 45 degrees by default, mode orthogonal keeps right angles | `from_n`, `from_p`, `layer` (optional), `mode` (optional), `to_n`, `to_p`, `width` (optional) |
| `footprint.mirror` | Mirror a board footprint left-to-right or top-to-bottom about its own origin | `axis`, `id` |
| `pad.table` | Report every board pad: number, net, position, shape, size and drill, by component reference | `component` (optional) |
| `items.update` | Apply property changes to up to 128 placed board objects in one undo step: tracks take net, copper layer and width; vias take net, diameter and drill; labels take text, layer and size | `items` |
| `drill.chart` | Report the board's drilled holes grouped by size: every drilled via and through-hole pad counted per round diameter or oval width and height, with the board thickness |  |
| `board.statistics` | Report board counts and totals: footprints, tracks and routed copper length per layer, vias, zones split into poured and outline-only, cutouts, labels, drilled holes, board area and the recorded surface finish |  |
| `board.panel` | Report a panel layout for the current board: a grid of copies separated by chosen gaps with rails around the edge, giving the finished panel size and every copy origin, without changing the design | `columns`, `pitch_x`, `pitch_y`, `rail` (optional), `rows` |
| `panel.set` | Record manufacturing panel settings on the project: grid size, gaps, rails, tab channel width and separation method | `columns` (optional), `enabled` (optional), `pitch_x` (optional), `pitch_y` (optional), `rail` (optional), `rows` (optional), `separation` (optional), `tab_channel` (optional) |
| `panel.clear` | Turn off panel settings and return them to defaults |  |
| `panel.export` | Write panel fabrication files (duplicated gerbers, drill with breakaway and tooling holes, pick-and-place per copy) into a directory | `directory` |

| `board.reset_drill_origin` | Return the drill origin to the board's lower-left corner |  |

| `board.clear_outline` | Drop the traced board outline and return to the plain rectangular board |  |
| `board.set_layer_record` | Record or replace one board layer note: its name, role (copper, core, prepreg, soldermask, silkscreen, paste or custom) and thickness in millimetres; at most 32 notes per board | `kind`, `name`, `thickness` |

| `rules.exclude` | Silence one check code for particular design objects; a finding drops when every object it names is excluded | `code`, `ids` |
| `rules.include` | Lift object exclusions for one check code; omit ids to lift every exclusion of that code | `code`, `ids` (optional) |
| `rules.exclude_region` | Silence one check code inside a rectangle; a finding drops when every object it names sits within the region | `code`, `height`, `width`, `x`, `y` |
| `rules.include_region` | Lift rectangular region exclusions for one check code; omit index to lift every region of that code | `code`, `index` (optional) |

| `board.layer_dotted_set` | Draw a drawn layer as evenly spaced dots, the look of a perforation a board snaps along, or as a solid line again | `layer`, `on` |
| `board.layer_visible_set` | Show or hide a drawn layer on screen without deleting it | `layer`, `on` |
| `board.layer_delete` | Delete a drawn layer and every figure on it | `layer` |
| `board.layer_line_add` | Draw a straight stroke on a drawn layer, in board millimetres | `layer`, `x1`, `x2`, `y1`, `y2` |
| `board.layer_rect_add` | Draw a rectangle outline on a drawn layer | `height`, `layer`, `width`, `x`, `y` |
| `board.layer_circle_add` | Draw a circle outline on a drawn layer | `layer`, `radius`, `x`, `y` |
| `board.layer_poly_add` | Draw a closed outline through 2 to 64 points on a drawn layer | `layer`, `points` |

| `rules.area_remove` | Remove one rule area by id | `id` |
| `rules.profile_list` | List built-in interface rule profiles with id, name, category and summary |  |

| `output_job.remove` | Remove a recorded output job by name | `name` |

| `reference_image.set` | Move, rescale, fade or hide a reference picture | `id`, `opacity` (optional), `scale` (optional), `visible` (optional), `x` (optional), `y` (optional) |

| `image.trace` | Trace the dark parts of an attached PNG into closed outlines on a board target: silk_front, silk_back, mask_front, mask_back (board graphics with a fabrication sublayer), layer (a drawn machine layer, needs layer) or copper (a filled zone, needs net). Give either file with x, y and scale, or reference to reuse a reference picture's placement. Only the outer edge of each blob is traced, at most 32 blobs. An invalid trace changes nothing | `copper_layer` (optional), `file` (optional), `invert` (optional), `layer` (optional), `max_vertices` (optional), `net` (optional), `reference` (optional), `scale` (optional), `smooth` (optional), `target`, `threshold` (optional), `width` (optional), `x` (optional), `y` (optional) |
| `net.impedance` | Report the estimated single-ended microstrip impedance of each routed net from its widest track, the recorded stackup and the recorded copper thickness, with effective permittivity and delay per millimetre; a net in a differential pair also reports its differential impedance at the pair gap. With target (ohms) it also reports the width that would meet it by bisection on the same model, and target_diff does the same for the differential impedance | `net` (optional), `target` (optional), `target_diff` (optional) |
| `impedance.calc` | Pure impedance calculator for one geometry, touching nothing in the design: microstrip, coupled (edge-coupled pair, reports odd, even and differential), or stripline (strip centred between two planes, height is the plane to plane spacing); height and er default to the board stackup; with target it also solves the width by bisection | `er` (optional), `gap` (optional), `geometry`, `height` (optional), `target` (optional), `thickness` (optional), `width` |
| `board.set_length_group` | Declare a named length-match group of two to 32 nets whose routed lengths must stay within a tolerance of each other; the same name updates the group, and DRC reports a length_group_skew finding when the longest and shortest net differ by more than the tolerance | `id` (optional), `name`, `nets`, `tolerance` |
| `board.remove_length_group` | Remove a length-match group by id; the nets and their copper stay | `id` |
| `net.length_groups` | Report each length-match group: every net's routed length and delay, how far each falls short of the longest net, the spread, and whether the group is inside its tolerance; read only | `id` (optional) |
| `track.tune_length` | Replace one straight track with a serpentine so the net's total routed length reaches a target within a tolerance. Bumps rise on whichever side has room, legs are spaced at least three dielectric heights apart by default and no longer than fifteen heights, corners are 45 degree mitres or rounded. Refuses curved tracks, differential pair nets, nets already at or beyond the target, and runs with no clear room, leaving the design untouched. Reports before and after length and delay | `amplitude_max` (optional), `spacing` (optional), `style` (optional), `target`, `tolerance` (optional), `track` |
